item: Skill Runner for Local LLM Harness
best_architecture: A three-stage progressive-disclosure architecture mirroring Claude Code / obra/superpowers, adapted for a local Gemma 4 + Python orchestrator. STAGE 1 — DISCOVERY & CATALOG (eager, cheap): At harness startup, recursively scan layered filesystem roots in strict descending priority (project '.claude/skills/' or './skills/' > personal '~/.claude/skills/' > bundled/superpowers library). For each 'SKILL.md' parse ONLY the YAML frontmatter (name, description, allowed-tools, model, version, license) — never the body. Build an in-memory catalog: dict[name -> SkillMeta(path, description, frontmatter)]. On name collision, highest-priority tier wins (project overrides personal overrides bundled), exactly as superpowers resolves Project > Personal > Superpowers tiers. STAGE 2 — CATALOG INJECTION: Render the catalog (name + one-line description, ~100 tokens/skill) into the Gemma 4 system prompt as an index, AND expose a single native tool 'load_skill(name: str)'. This keeps context flat regardless of how many skills are installed — Gemma only sees that each skill exists and when it applies. STAGE 3 — LLM-MEDIATED ACTIVATION (lazy): The model decides relevance from descriptions and emits a load_skill tool call. The runner resolves name -> path (re-validating path confinement), reads and parses the SKILL.md body lazily, and returns the body text as the tool_response. The body then lives in context and steers subsequent turns. Helper assets / reference files / scripts referenced by the skill are loaded a third level deeper, only when the skill body instructs the model to read or execute them. KEY DECISIONS: (1) Lazy body loading is the single most important decision — it decouples catalog size from context cost. (2) Use the LLM as the router (a load_skill tool call) rather than embedding-similarity retrieval, because Gemma 4 has native function-calling tokens and descriptions are written precisely for trigger matching; keep embedding retrieval as an optional fallback for very large libraries (Voyager-style top-k). (3) Treat the catalog as data injected each turn but the skill body as a one-time tool result — so deactivation is simply not re-appending it. (4) Run the whole thing inside a ReAct loop (thought -> load_skill / tool -> observation -> next thought) so skills can chain: a loaded skill body can instruct the model to load another skill, enabling composition. (5) Separate the read-only 'instruction' skills (markdown that steers the model) from 'executable' skills (markdown that ships scripts) — the latter route through a sandboxed subprocess runner, the former are pure context injection. (6) Make discovery hot-reloadable (re-scan on filesystem change) so authoring new skills doesn't require a harness restart, matching superpowers' session-start auto-update.
reference_papers: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models (Wang et al. 2023) - arxiv:2305.16291 - the canonical 'ever-growing skill library' design: skills are executable code added to a library on successful self-verification, each indexed by an embedding of its description, with top-5 semantic retrieval at task time; directly informs lazy skill cataloging, retrieval-augmented activation, and skill composition for a local agent.

ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models (Yao et al. 2022) - arxiv:2210.03629 - the thought->action->observation loop that the skill runner's activation cycle should implement; load_skill is an 'action' whose returned body is an 'observation' that reshapes the next thought.

Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools (Schick et al. 2023) - arxiv:2302.04761 - foundational treatment of LLM-mediated tool invocation via in-context API calls, relevant to framing load_skill as a first-class tool.

Gorilla: Large Language Model Connected with Massive APIs (Patil et al. 2023) - arxiv:2305.15334 - retrieval-aware tool/API selection at scale; relevant if the skill catalog grows beyond what fits a prompt and needs a retriever in front of load_skill.

Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior (Park et al. 2023) - arxiv:2304.03442 - memory stream / retrieval architecture patterns applicable to skill memory and selective context injection.

MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems (Packer et al. 2023) - arxiv:2310.08560 - tiered/paged context management; the analogy of paging skill bodies in and out of the limited Gemma context window mirrors MemGPT's virtual context.

CodeAct / Executable Code Actions Elicit Better LLM Agents (Wang et al. 2024) - arxiv:2402.01030 - argues code-as-action outperforms JSON tool calls for compositional tasks; informs the design of executable (script-bearing) skills versus pure-instruction skills.

SkillFlow: Scalable and Efficient Agent Skill Retrieval System (2025) - arxiv:2504.06188 - retrieves higher-level PROCEDURAL knowledge as structured SKILL.md bundles (multi-step instructions + scripts + references) rather than atomic API signatures; the closest published analogue to a SKILL.md runner's retrieval layer and validates the bundle-as-unit design.

Tool-to-Agent Retrieval: Bridging Tools and Agents for Scalable LLM Multi-Agent Systems (2025) - arxiv:2511.01854 - embeds both tools and parent agents in a shared vector space linked via metadata; reports +19.4% Recall@5 and +17.7% nDCG@5 over prior agent retrievers on LiveMCPBench. Directly informs an embedding-retrieval fallback that scales load_skill routing past keyword/description matching without context dilution.

SkillRouter: Retrieve-and-Rerank Skill Selection for LLM Agents at Scale (2026) - arxiv:2603.22455 - key finding: in large, highly-overlapping skill pools, name+description alone is INSUFFICIENT for routing and the FULL skill body is the decisive signal. The routing layer can inspect full text while the consuming agent sees only name+description; argues for a retrieve-then-rerank stage over body text before activation.
reference_repos: obra/superpowers - the reference Claude Code skills framework: 14 SKILL.md files (TDD, debugging, brainstorming, writing-plans, code-review, verification) + session-start bootstrap hook + per-host plugin manifests; defines the discovery/parse/resolve algorithm and Project>Personal>Superpowers tier precedence to port from - https://github.com/obra/superpowers (skills now split into obra/superpowers-skills)

anthropics/claude-code - canonical SKILL.md format, frontmatter fields (name, description, disable-model-invocation, allowed-tools), and the skill-development meta-skill that documents progressive disclosure and the <500-line body guideline - https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code (see plugins/plugin-dev/skills/skill-development/SKILL.md)

MineDojo/Voyager - reference implementation of an ever-growing skill library with embedding-indexed retrieval, skill composition, and self-verification before adding a skill; the SkillManager class is the closest analog to a Python skill runner with a vector store - https://github.com/MineDojo/Voyager

agent0ai/agent-zero - fully prompt/markdown-driven agentic framework where behavior lives in prompts/*.md and dynamic tools live in python/tools/; Docker-based sandboxed code execution and 'works with very small models' tool-calling parser are directly relevant to a Gemma-4 local harness - https://github.com/agent0ai/agent-zero

sst/opencode - multi-host agent that consumes the same superpowers SKILL.md files; its skills discovery resolves .opencode/skills/ (project) > ~/.config/opencode/skills/ (personal) > bundled, a clean reference for layered-root resolution outside Claude Code - https://github.com/sst/opencode

eyeseast/python-frontmatter - the library to use for parsing/serializing YAML frontmatter (safe mode by default; frontmatter.parse() returns (metadata, content) so you can grab frontmatter-only cheaply) - https://github.com/eyeseast/python-frontmatter

unslothai/unsloth - the inference/fine-tune stack for Gemma 4; chat_templates.py and the FunctionGemma tutorials show how apply_chat_template(tools=...) renders native tool-call tokens for local function calling - https://github.com/unslothai/unsloth
key_libraries: python-frontmatter (Python, >=1.1.0) - primary frontmatter parser; frontmatter.load(file)/loads(text) return a Post with .metadata (dict) and .content (str), frontmatter.parse(text) returns (metadata, content) tuple for cheap catalog-only parsing; uses yaml.safe_load under the hood by default. Use for both discovery (frontmatter-only) and activation (body).

PyYAML (Python, >=6.0) - dependency of python-frontmatter; if implementing manually use yaml.safe_load ONLY (never yaml.load / FullLoader on untrusted skill files) to prevent arbitrary object instantiation. Pair with content.split('---', 2) for a zero-dependency fallback parser.

transformers (Python, >=4.57 for Gemma 4 support) - provides AutoProcessor/AutoTokenizer.apply_chat_template(messages, tools=tools, add_generation_prompt=True) which renders Gemma 4's native function-calling tokens; tools are passed as OpenAI-format JSON Schema or as plain Python callables (auto-introspected).

unsloth (Python, latest) - fast local Gemma 4 inference + fine-tuning; get_chat_template(tokenizer, chat_template='gemma-3'/'gemma-4') and its tool-calling templates. Use unsloth/gemma-4-* or functiongemma builds which ship the function-calling system prompt pre-baked.
pathlib (Python stdlib) - Path.resolve().is_relative_to(base) for path-confinement of skill roots and referenced assets (Python 3.9+; is_relative_to added in 3.9).

pydantic (Python, v2) - validate/normalize parsed frontmatter into a typed SkillMeta model (required name+description, optional allowed-tools, version, model, license); reject malformed skills early with clear errors.
watchfiles or watchdog (Python) - optional, for hot-reload: re-scan skill roots on filesystem changes so newly authored skills appear without restart.

sentence-transformers / faiss-cpu or chromadb (Python) - OPTIONAL fallback retriever for very large skill libraries (Voyager-style top-k by description embedding) when the full catalog no longer fits the system prompt.

subprocess + os (stdlib) / or a microsandbox (Docker, bubblewrap, or seccomp wrapper) - for executing script-bearing skills with cleared env vars, dropped capabilities, temp working dir, and a timeout.
pitfalls: Loading skill bodies eagerly into the system prompt. This defeats progressive disclosure and blows the (smaller) Gemma context budget after only a handful of skills. Parse frontmatter ONLY at discovery; load the body strictly on load_skill activation.

Using yaml.load() / yaml.FullLoader instead of yaml.safe_load on skill frontmatter. Skill files are user/community content (especially when porting superpowers); the unsafe loader can instantiate arbitrary Python objects. Always safe_load (python-frontmatter does this by default — don't override it).

No path confinement on skill names or referenced assets. A load_skill('../../etc/passwd') or a skill body that reads '../../../secret' is a directory-traversal vector. Canonicalize with Path.resolve() and verify is_relative_to(allowed_root) AFTER resolving symlinks; never do naive '../' substring checks (bypassable as foo/../../..). Validate the resolved real path against each allowed root.

Assuming Gemma 3 and Gemma 4 have the same tool-calling mechanics. Gemma 3 has NO dedicated tool tokens (function calling is pure prompt engineering / JSON-in-prompt) whereas Gemma 4 ships native function-calling special tokens (<|tool_call>call:NAME{ARGS}<tool_call|> and tool_response tokens). If the spec targets 'Gemma 4', lean on apply_chat_template(tools=...) and the native handshake; if any component falls back to Gemma 3, you must parse JSON tool calls out of free text yourself.

Parsing Gemma 4 tool calls naively. Known issue: some runtimes (llama-cpp-python) return Gemma 4 tool calls as raw native tokens inside 'content' rather than a structured tool_calls field unless the correct jinja template is used (llama.cpp needs --jinja; vLLM needs --enable-auto-tool-choice). Validate that your inference path actually emits structured calls before trusting the parser.

Treating the description field as documentation rather than the routing signal. The description is the SINGLE most important field — it is what Gemma matches against to decide load_skill. A vague description means the skill never triggers or triggers on everything. Enforce the 'what it does + when to use it + key capabilities' formula at authoring/validation time.

Letting skill bodies grow unbounded. Once loaded a body persists in context across turns (recurring token cost). Enforce the <500-line guideline and push detail into separate reference files loaded a level deeper (third-tier disclosure).

No collision-resolution rule across the layered roots. Without a defined precedence, project-local overrides of a personal/bundled skill silently fail or double-register. Implement strict Project > Personal > Bundled precedence and surface a warning on shadowing.

Executing script-bearing skills in-process or with the full parent environment. Run them in a subprocess with env scrubbed (env={} or a minimal allowlist), a confined temp cwd, a wall-clock timeout, and ideally dropped Linux capabilities / a container. Never exec untrusted skill scripts directly in the orchestrator process.

Unbounded ReAct / skill-chaining loops. A skill that loads another skill that loads the first can loop, and appended observations grow context until it overflows. Cap iterations, dedupe already-loaded skills, and compact/evict stale skill bodies (MemGPT-style) for long-horizon tasks.

Re-reading the whole SKILL.md (frontmatter + body) on every discovery scan. For large libraries this is slow; use frontmatter.parse on a bounded read or stop reading after the closing '---' to keep startup cheap.
bdd_gherkin_scenarios:
Feature: Layered skill discovery and cataloging
  As the local Gemma 4 harness
  I want to discover skills from project, personal, and bundled roots
  So that the model has a catalog of available skills without paying body-token cost

  Scenario: Discover skills across all roots parsing frontmatter only
    Given a personal root "~/.claude/skills" containing "web-search/SKILL.md"
    And a project root "./.claude/skills" containing "deploy/SKILL.md"
    And each SKILL.md has valid YAML frontmatter with name and description
    When the skill runner performs discovery at startup
    Then the catalog contains entries "web-search" and "deploy"
    And each catalog entry holds only name, description, and resolved path
    And no skill body has been read into memory

  Scenario: Skip and warn on malformed frontmatter
    Given a skill file with frontmatter missing the required "description" field
    When the skill runner performs discovery
    Then that skill is excluded from the catalog
    And a warning naming the offending file path is logged
    And discovery of all other skills still succeeds

Feature: Collision resolution by tier precedence
  As the skill runner
  I want project skills to override personal and bundled skills of the same name
  So that local customizations win deterministically

  Scenario: Project tier overrides personal tier on name collision
    Given a personal skill "deploy" at "~/.claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md"
    And a project skill "deploy" at "./.claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md"
    When discovery resolves the name "deploy"
    Then the catalog entry "deploy" points to the project-tier path
    And a shadowing warning identifies the overridden personal-tier path

Feature: Lazy LLM-mediated skill activation via load_skill
  As the harness orchestrator
  I want the model to activate a skill by emitting a load_skill tool call
  So that the body is loaded only when relevant

  Scenario: Model loads a skill body on demand
    Given the catalog is injected into the Gemma 4 system prompt
    And a single tool "load_skill(name)" is exposed via apply_chat_template(tools=...)
    When the model emits a tool call load_skill with name "deploy"
    Then the runner resolves "deploy" to its confined path
    And reads and parses the SKILL.md body
    And returns the body text as the tool_response for the next turn
    And the catalog injection remains unchanged in size

  Scenario: Activation of an unknown skill is rejected gracefully
    When the model emits a tool call load_skill with name "does-not-exist"
    Then the runner returns a tool_response error "unknown skill: does-not-exist"
    And the available skill names are listed in the error
    And no file read is attempted

Feature: Path confinement and safe parsing security
  As a security-conscious skill runner
  I want to confine all file access to allowed roots and parse YAML safely
  So that malicious skill names or content cannot escape the sandbox

  Scenario: Reject directory traversal in a skill name
    Given allowed roots "~/.claude/skills" and "./.claude/skills"
    When the model emits load_skill with name "../../../../etc/passwd"
    Then the resolved real path is checked with is_relative_to against every allowed root
    And because it is outside all roots the request is rejected
    And no file outside the allowed roots is opened

  Scenario: Frontmatter is parsed with a safe loader
    Given a SKILL.md whose frontmatter contains a YAML tag like "!!python/object/apply:os.system"
    When the runner parses the frontmatter
    Then yaml.safe_load is used so the tag is not constructed into an object
    And parsing either yields plain data or raises a handled error
    And no arbitrary code is executed during parsing

Feature: Skill chaining within the ReAct loop
  As an agent solving a multi-step task
  I want a loaded skill to be able to trigger loading another skill
  So that skills compose without preloading everything

  Scenario: Chained activation with loop and dedupe guards
    Given skill "writing-plans" whose body instructs loading "test-driven-development"
    When the model loads "writing-plans" and then emits load_skill "test-driven-development"
    Then both bodies are present in context
    And re-emitting load_skill for an already-loaded skill returns a cached note instead of re-appending the body
    And the activation loop halts after the configured maximum iteration count
sota_improvements: Use Gemma 4's NATIVE function-calling tokens for load_skill instead of prompt-engineered JSON. Pass the tool via apply_chat_template(tools=[load_skill_schema]) and parse the structured <|tool_call>call:load_skill{...}<tool_call|> handshake; this is materially more reliable than Gemma 3-style JSON-in-prompt and removes brittle regex extraction. Verify the inference backend (llama.cpp --jinja, vLLM --enable-auto-tool-choice) actually emits structured calls.

Add an embedding-retrieval fallback in front of load_skill (Voyager-style): when the catalog exceeds a token budget, retrieve top-k skills by description embedding and inject only those names into the prompt, keeping load_skill as the activation primitive. Best of both: precise LLM routing for small libraries, scalable retrieval for large ones.

Retrieve-then-rerank over FULL skill bodies for large, overlapping libraries (SkillRouter, arxiv:2603.22455): the routing layer can inspect each skill's full body even though the model only sees name+description, and the body is the decisive routing signal when many descriptions overlap. Shortlist by description embedding, then rerank the candidates against the query using body text before deciding which name(s) to surface to load_skill — recovers routing accuracy that name+description matching alone loses at scale (cf. Tool-to-Agent Retrieval +19.4% Recall@5).

Graph-of-Skills dependency-aware activation: let SKILL.md frontmatter declare prerequisite skills; on activation the runner auto-loads the transitive dependency closure in topological order, guarded by the existing visited-set + max-chain cycle guard, so composed skills work without the model having to discover and load each prerequisite manually.

Tiered/paged context management for skill bodies (MemGPT-inspired): evict or summarize stale loaded skill bodies once a turn budget is exceeded so long-horizon ReAct tasks don't overflow Gemma's window; keep a compact 'skills currently active' memory rather than appending every body forever.

Self-verification and an ever-growing local skill library (Voyager): let the harness WRITE new SKILL.md files when a task is solved and self-verified, auto-generating frontmatter (name + description) and persisting to the project root, so the agent's capability set compounds across sessions.

Separate executable skills into a hardened sandbox tier: run script-bearing skills in a subprocess with scrubbed env, confined temp cwd, wall-clock timeout, and dropped Linux capabilities (or a container/bubblewrap), distinct from pure-instruction skills that are mere context injection.

Author-time skill validation/linting: enforce the description formula ('what it does + when to use it + key capabilities'), the <500-line body guideline, required frontmatter fields via a pydantic model, and a frontmatter-only readability check — fail fast at discovery with actionable messages.
Hot-reload via filesystem watching (watchfiles) so newly authored or git-auto-updated skills appear without a harness restart; re-run discovery on change events.

Add an allowed-tools enforcement layer: honor the SKILL.md 'allowed-tools' frontmatter so that when a skill is active the harness restricts which other tools the model may call, matching Claude Code semantics and tightening the security envelope.
